[1, 5] [6, 7] <4> The U.S. energy storage market set a new quarterly record in the second quarter of 2023, installing 5,597 megawatt-hours (MWh) of new capacity. [8] The conference showcased innovations across the clean energy spectrum, including solar (Solar Power International), energy storage (Energy Storage International), wind, hydrogen, fuel cells, electric vehicles, and microgrids. [2] Key discussions revolved around the impact of the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), which is anticipated to add $565 billion to the U.S. economy over the next decade. [8] The event also featured 370 educational sessions and an expansive expo hall with industry leaders like Tesla, Schneider Electric, and Panasonic. [2, 11] <6> On September 7, 2023, Wood Mackenzie and the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA) jointly released the U.S. Solar Market Insight Q3 2023 report. The report details that the U.S. solar market installed 5.6 GWdc of capacity in the second quarter of 2023, which is a 20% increase compared to the same quarter in 2022. It projects that the U.S. will add a record 32 GW of new solar capacity in 2023, a 52% increase from the previous year. A significant driver of future growth is the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), which has spurred dozens of announcements for new domestic module manufacturing facilities. If these plans are realized, U.S. solar module manufacturing capacity is expected to increase tenfold by 2026, from 10.6 GW to 108.5 GW. The report also identifies challenges facing the industry, including pipeline stagnation due to high interest rates, elevated hardware and labor costs, and increased local opposition to clean energy projects. <7> The Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM) held the first-ever offshore wind energy auction for the Gulf of Mexico on August 29, 2023. In the auction, RWE Offshore US Gulf, LLC was the sole winner, securing the 102,480-acre Lake Charles Lease Area. The company submitted a winning bid of $5.6 million for the area, which has a potential generating capacity of 1.24 gigawatts. <8> On August 29, 2023, the U.S. Department of the Treasury and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) issued proposed regulations to provide guidance on the prevailing wage and registered apprenticeship requirements included in the Inflation Reduction Act. [1, 4] These rules are intended to ensure clean energy projects create good-paying jobs by requiring taxpayers to meet these standards to qualify for enhanced tax benefits. [1, 4] Satisfying the requirements can increase the value of a tax credit or deduction by up to five times the base amount. [4] The guidance specifies the required percentages of labor hours that must be performed by qualified apprentices and clarifies that workers must be paid wages at or above the prevailing rates determined by the U.S. Department of Labor for their geographic area and type of work. [2, 4] <9> The U.S. Department of the Interior announced its approval for the construction and operation of the Revolution Wind project offshore Rhode Island on August 22, 2023. Located approximately 15 nautical miles southeast of Point Judith, the project is designed to have an estimated capacity of 704 megawatts, which is enough to power nearly 250,000 homes. The project is anticipated to create around 1,200 local jobs during its construction phase. Revolution Wind is the first multi-state offshore wind project in the United States, set to provide 400 MW of power to Rhode Island and 304 MW to Connecticut. The new regulations establish an annual capacity allocation of 225 MW for the 2024 energy year. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> MN8 Energy, one of the largest independent renewable energy companies in the U.S. and a spin-off from Goldman Sachs Asset Management, announced the closing of its first private placement on April 1, 2024, raising $325 million. [2] The investment consists of $200 million from Mercuria Energy Group, a global energy and commodity group, and $125 million from infrastructure investor Ridgewood Infrastructure. [2, 3] The funds, raised through the sale of convertible preferred stock, are intended to support MN8's expanded operations and growth plans. [1, 2] As part of the agreement, Mercuria secured one seat and an observer seat on MN8's board of directors, while Ridgewood received an observer seat. [1, 2] The deal also initiated a strategic collaboration between MN8 and Mercuria to identify commercial opportunities for advancing sustainable energy systems. [2, 6] <2> In January 2024, solar energy constituted 87.3% of new electricity generating capacity in the United States, with the addition of 2.527 gigawatts. [1] This information is based on data from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission's (FERC) "Energy Infrastructure Update," which included data through January 31, 2024. [1] The significant contribution of solar power in the first month of the year marked a strong start for the renewables sector. [1] In total, renewable energy sources were responsible for 98.3% of all new capacity added in January. [1] <3> In March 2024, Walmart announced an expansion of its partnership with Nexamp to support 26 new community solar projects across six states. This initiative is expected to generate enough electricity to provide energy bill savings for approximately 13,000 residential households annually. <4> The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) released Notice 2024-30 on March 22, 2024, which expands the rules and updates the lists for designating an 'energy community.' This guidance is significant for developers of renewable energy projects who are looking to qualify for a 10% bonus tax credit for projects situated in these areas, as provided for by the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA). The notice also includes appendices that identify additional Metropolitan Statistical Areas (MSAs) and non-MSAs that now meet the criteria for an energy community based on fossil fuel employment and unemployment rate requirements. <5> The South Fork Wind project, a joint venture by Ørsted and Eversource, is the first utility-scale offshore wind farm in U.S. federal waters. Located approximately 35 miles east of Montauk Point, New York, the project consists of 12 turbines with a total capacity of around 132 MW, enough to power about 70,000 homes. The project achieved a significant milestone on December 6, 2023, when it began delivering its first power to the Long Island grid. Construction and commissioning continued, and in March 2024, Governor Kathy Hochul and other officials announced the project's official completion, with all 12 turbines fully operational and supplying power. <6> The U.S. solar market set a new record in 2023, installing 32.4 gigawatts (GW) of new capacity, a 51% increase from 2022. This growth was largely driven by the utility-scale sector, which installed over 10 GW in the fourth quarter alone. Overall, solar represented 53% of all new electricity-generating capacity added to the U.S. grid during the year. Every market segment experienced year-over-year growth, bringing the total installed solar capacity in the United States to 177 GW. The record-breaking year is partly attributed to the stabilization of the module supply chain, allowing projects delayed in 2022 to be completed. <7> On March 1, 2024, Vistra Corp. announced it had completed its acquisition of Energy Harbor Corp. [1]. The deal expands Vistra's portfolio of zero-carbon electricity generation by adding approximately 4,000 megawatts of 24/7 nuclear generation capacity and about 1 million retail customers. [1] With this acquisition, Vistra now operates the second-largest competitive nuclear fleet in the United States. [1, 4] <8> The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) made two separate announcements regarding significant funding for enhanced geothermal systems (EGS). On January 30, 2024, the DOE's Geothermal Technologies Office announced a funding opportunity of up to $31 million for projects to support EGS wellbore tools and the use of low-temperature geothermal heat for industrial processes. Subsequently, on February 13, 2024, the DOE announced the selection of three pilot projects to receive up to $60 million to demonstrate the effectiveness and scalability of EGS. These projects, funded by the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, are located in Sonoma County, California (Chevron New Energies); the Milford Renewable Energy Corridor in Utah (Fervo Energy); and on Newberry Volcano in Oregon (Mazama Energy). The goal of these pilot demonstrations is to advance geothermal power into new regions and support the DOE's Enhanced Geothermal Shot initiative, which aims to reduce the cost of EGS by 90% by 2035. <9> Geothermal energy company Fervo Energy announced it has reduced drilling times by 70% for its enhanced geothermal system (EGS) wells at its Cape Station project in Beaver County, Utah. [2, 3] The company reported that its fastest well was drilled in just 21 days, a significant improvement from its first horizontal well drilled in 2022. [2, 5] This increased efficiency led to a substantial cost reduction, with the price per well dropping from $9.4 million to $4.8 million. [2, 3, 4] The drilling campaign at the 400 MW Cape Station project began in June 2023. [2, 3, 5] The advancements are attributed to a repeatable drilling process that allows for continuous improvement. [2, 5]

The total generation for the year was 425,235 gigawatt-hours (GWh), a 2.1% drop from the 434,297 GWh produced in 2022. This decline occurred despite the addition of 6.2 gigawatts (GW) of new wind capacity during 2023, which brought the national total to 147.5 GW. The primary reason for the reduced output was slower-than-average wind speeds, particularly in the first half of the year, which saw a 14% drop in generation compared to the same period in 2022. Some experts attribute the weaker winds to the El Niño climate pattern. The decrease in generation was not uniform across the country; the upper Midwest experienced the most significant declines, while Texas, the state with the largest wind capacity, saw a 4.4% increase. The national average capacity factor for the wind turbine fleet fell to 33.5%, an eight-year low. <2> The U.S. Department of the Interior, through the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM) and the Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE), announced a final rule to update regulations for renewable energy development on the U.S. Outer Continental Shelf. [3, 6] Known as the Renewable Energy Modernization Rule, it aims to encourage offshore wind development by modernizing regulations, streamlining complex processes, reducing administrative burdens, and enhancing compliance. [3] The agencies anticipate that these updates will save the industry an estimated US$1 billion over the next 20 years. [3] Key changes include eliminating unnecessary requirements for meteorological buoys, increasing survey flexibility, improving the project design and installation verification process, and establishing a public Renewable Energy Leasing Schedule. [2] The rule also reforms BOEM's auction regulations and tailors financial assurance requirements. [2] This is the first major update to offshore wind regulations since they were established in 2009. [4] <3> On April 24, 2024, the U.S. Department of the Interior announced a new five-year offshore wind leasing schedule, detailing plans for up to 12 potential lease sales through 2028. The announcement was made by Secretary Deb Haaland at the International Partnering Forum conference in New Orleans. The Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM) anticipates future lease sales in the Atlantic, Gulf of Mexico, Pacific, and waters offshore of U.S. territories. The schedule outlines one potential sale in the Gulf of Mexico for 2025, with a total of four sales planned for 2024, one in 2026, two in 2027, and four in 2028. <4> In its Q1 2024 U.S. Offshore Wind Quarterly Market Report, the Oceantic Network announced that the total approved capacity for offshore wind construction in the United States had surpassed 10 GW. The report, which covers industry developments for the first three months of 2024, highlighted that the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM) had increased the total capacity approved for construction by over 30% during this period. <5> A report titled "The 50 States of Solar" from the NC Clean Energy Technology Center (NCCETC) for the first quarter of 2024 found that 43 states, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico took a total of 163 distributed solar policy actions. The most common actions were related to net metering policies, with 56 actions taken. This was followed by 42 actions concerning residential fixed charge or minimum bill increases and 37 actions related to community solar policies. The report, covering the period ending March 31, 2024, was published on April 17, 2024. <6> On April 17, 2024, a coalition of nearly 200 solar and energy storage companies sent a letter to U.S. congressional leaders urging the passage of legislative reforms. The letter specifically advocated for modernizing and streamlining federal energy permitting, creating project siting partnerships across all levels of government, investing in the build-out and modernization of transmission capacity, and simplifying the process for clean energy projects to gain access to public lands. <7> An article published on April 15, 2024, citing forecasts from the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), predicted a significant increase in the United States' renewable energy capacity for the year 2024. The forecast anticipated the addition of over 67 gigawatts (GW) of new renewable capacity. Solar energy is expected to be the primary driver of this growth, accounting for more than 56 GW of the new capacity. Other forecasts from the EIA support this trend, projecting that renewables will represent 23% of U.S. electricity generation in 2024. Specifically, the EIA expects 37 GW of solar capacity to be added during the year. While figures vary slightly between analyses, a consensus exists that solar power is leading the substantial expansion of renewable energy in the U.S. throughout 2024. <8> The U.S. Department of the Interior announced that the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) has permitted nearly 29 gigawatts of clean energy projects on public lands, surpassing its 25-gigawatt goal ahead of the 2025 deadline. [7, 9] This achievement includes solar, wind, and geothermal projects, enough to power over 12 million homes. [9] Coinciding with this milestone, the Department of the Interior issued a final rule from the BLM designed to promote further renewable energy development. [9] This new rule will reduce capacity fees for wind and solar projects by 80%, streamline the application process, and offer additional incentives for projects that use American-made materials or project labor agreements. [3, 4] The BLM is currently processing permits for an additional 66 utility-scale clean energy projects. [6]

[2, 3] Site mobilization for the project began in mid-July 2025, with civil work underway in partnership with Brooks Construction. [2, 3, 4] In a statement, Nick Sylvestre, Founder and CEO of Louth Callan Renewables, said, “We’re excited to bring our construction expertise to another large solar project in the New England region.” [2, 3, 4] As the EPC lead, LCR is responsible for all aspects of the project, including engineering, procurement, environmental compliance, construction, and final commissioning, which is anticipated by the third quarter of 2026. The policy change is expected to create significant uncertainty and cause delays for renewable energy projects that are on federal land or require DOI approval for activities on private land.
